passage:
Before the singing contest, Anna caught a cold and lost her voice. She had practiced for weeks and felt unlucky.
Her teacher suggested that she still join the contest as a stage helper. Anna agreed, though she was disappointed.
On contest day, she helped performers find microphones, carried water, and calmed nervous students. She saw how much work happened behind the stage.
After the contest, the teacher thanked her in front of everyone. Anna did not sing, but she had helped the show succeed.
Her voice returned a few days later. She still wanted to sing next year, but she had learned something important: a performance needs more than performers. Quiet support can also deserve applause.
